summary: In the United States, ibuprofen carries a boxed warning for stomach and gut harm, nerve system damage (neurotoxicity), and heart harm [3]. The drug also has warnings for severe allergic reactions—which can cause symptoms such as hives, facial swelling, asthma, shock, or blisters—as well as stomach bleeding [7]. Additionally, a small computer model, rather than tests on people, calculated low risk scores for ibuprofen's effects on the liver and heart [M]. Similar drugs also have warnings or history of removal from the market for liver harm, heart harm, digestive tract harm, and nerve system damage [4][5][6].
